summary: tools/voice/score.py and tools/voice/tests/test_score.py written. 17 plain assert tests pass (pytest is not in .venv-audio, so the file runs as a script and is pytest-compatible). Real end-to-end run on kitten/cpu (15/15 lines, Whisper small on cuda via the lock): median WER 0.050, worst 0.167, names 13/24; listening copies for 4 listen lines made.
digit_handling: The Whisper normaliser alone fails the required cases: it turns 'seven four niner' into '74 niner', drops the zero of 'pad 04' (-> 4) and the percent sign of '20 %', and 'seven four nine' into 749. score.py therefore adds an explicit step: before the normaliser niner->nine, decimal->point, m/s->metres per second, % -> percent, every digit string spelled out as spoken digits, possessive names kept whole (normaliser turns Drover's into 'drover is'); after it every digit run is cut into single digit tokens. Tested equal: seven four niner / 749 / 7 4 9 / seven four nine; five zero / 50; one one eight decimal three / 118.3; pad zero four / pad 04; 20 % / 20 percent; 62%; 95,000. A dropped zero or a wrong digit still counts as an error. Also NATO spelling 'Alpha Kilo' equals 'AK' / 'AK-447' (only where the reference spells it with NATO words).
error_split: Edit-distance alignment (diagonal preferred). Consecutive error ops form a run; a run touching a name position in the reference counts for the name (so a name heard as two words adds no ordinary error), other runs count as ordinary substitutions/deletions/insertions. name hit = name tokens all equal. Names that never appear in the normalised reference are not counted (names_in_reference).
level_notes: Loudness uses pyloudnorm at the file's own rate (synth/levels.py lufs() meters at fixed 48 kHz and tiles short clips, so it was not reused); true peak uses the same 4x resample_poly method as levels.py. transcribe.Whisper from tools/audio/listen reused by import; radio_filter from tools/audio/synth/radio.py reused by import. Silence = 10 ms windows below -50 dBFS RMS.
listen_copies: 48 kHz mono PCM_24, -23 LUFS target with true peak cut to <= -3 dBFS (gain reduced if needed, flagged 'limited'), 8 ms raised-cosine fades. Radio lines: filter applied after the loudness match, dry kept as __dry.wav. The radio filter changes loudness slightly (kitten radio_clearance -22.6 LUFS after the filter); only the gain-only peak guard is applied after it, no second loudness match, as the task order says. Best device = cuda timing.json if present else cpu.
scores_json: assets/audio/voice/scores.json is merged per model, so --models a run does not delete other models. Model directories starting with . or _ are skipped, therefore a fake model under _fake/ would be skipped; the end-to-end test used a temporary root (--root, hidden option) and a temp dir, then removed it (assets/audio/voice/_fake_score_tmp deleted).
whisper_tested: Yes, once on kitten/cpu through with_lock.py (waited 572 s for the lock); Whisper ran on cuda, load 0.8 s.
problems: pytest is not installed in .venv-audio; tests are plain functions runnable as a script.
Whisper small mishears invented names and some ordinary words, so WER mixes model errors and recogniser errors; numbers sort the field only.
notVerified: Timing key names for peak GPU memory in other adapters' timing.json: summary copies all scalar top-level keys under timing.all_scalars rather than naming one.
Behaviour on a model that writes stereo or int16 WAV beyond the synthetic tests (stereo is averaged to mono; tested only with mono floats).
The kitten run's scores.json and _listen copies are real outputs of one model; other models were mid-run and not scored.
